opennyai_summary.19_January_2018__PREAMBLE:
Mukesh Verma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr on 19
January, 2018
The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 Cra-1252-2017
 (Mukesh Verma Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr)
3
Gwalior, Dated : 19-01-2018
Shri B.K.Sharma, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State.
This appeal is though filed under Section 76 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006, however,
there is non-compliance of provision contained under sub section 1 of section 76 which contemplates the deposit of the amount imposed by way of penalty or compensation or damage.
opennyai_summary.19_January_2018__decision:
Let compliance be effected within fifteen days, failing which the appeal shall stand dismissed without further reference to the Court.
In case the compliance is effected, let the matter be set out for hearing on admission in the week commencing 5.2.2018.
opennyai_summary.final__PREAMBLE: Mukesh Verma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr on 27 February, 2018 THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH CRA-1252-2017 (MUKESH VERMA Vs THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THR) Gwalior, Dated : 27-02-2018 Parties as before.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Learned counsel for the appellant prays for and is granted time to convert the present appeal u/S 76(1) into an appeal u/S 71(6) of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.
sh For the said purpose no separate application shall be required.
e Petitioner is directed to carry out the amendment within two days.
ad If the amendment is carried out then Registery is directed to place this matter for admission before the appropriate Bench.
